threePreExistingTestsThatBrokeMidRemedia.symptom: After the DEFECT 1 provenance fix, the cross-origin navigate was no longer refused with INJECTION_INFLUENCE, so it reached GATE 5 and the run parked in NEEDS_USER_CONFIRMATION instead of FAILED.
threePreExistingTestsThatBrokeMidRemedia.rootCause: Two separate things were going on. (1) The ONLY reason those runs were blocked upstream was the DEFECT 1 false positive: the critic was running the page-hijack signature /navigate to/i over the model's own reason text ('Navigate to the requested site'). Fixing DEFECT 1 correctly removed that block. (2) securityCritic.ts:262 decides the cross-origin question from `goal`, which is task PLUS the planner's MODEL-AUTHORED subgoal narration. The subgoal in that run was 'Navigate to search engine or knowledge portal', so hasAnyTerm(goal, NAVIGATE_TERMS) was true and the cross-origin rule stood down. A subgoal the model itself wrote was vouching for an off-origin destination the user never named.
threePreExistingTestsThatBrokeMidRemedia.fix: securityCritic.ts now judges the cross-origin navigation rule from the USER'S TASK alone (`userGoal`), never from the model's own subgoal narration. This TIGHTENS the rule: it restores the pre-remediation refusal, and it keeps the security authority rather than weakening it. Goal-alignment questions still use the blended goal, because usefulness is a different question from safety.

securityPosture.netChange: The navigate is still refused. It is refused by the cross-origin rule again, which is the EARLIER gate, rather than by a downstream confirmation prompt.
securityPosture.note: The DEFECT 1 false positive was doing security work it was never designed to do. Relying on it meant the real rule had been silently disabled. It is now enforced in its own right.
